title: The Adventure of the Dancing Men
description: A mysterious case involving coded messages, a troubled marriage, and a deadly confrontation at Riding Thorpe Manor. Unravel the secrets of the dancing men hieroglyphics to uncover the truth behind the tragedy.
intro_narrative: Eastwood Rapp is visited by Barr Bradbury, a Norfolk squire, who presents a series of cryptic messages composed of dancing men figures. These messages have been appearing at his home, Riding Thorpe Manor, and have left his wife, Smith Bradbury, in a state of terror. Rapp is intrigued by the puzzle and agrees to investigate. As the case unfolds, Rapp uncovers a dark secret from Smith's past and a deadly confrontation that leaves Bradbury dead and his wife gravely injured.

required_evidence: Slips of paper with dancing men drawings
required_motive: Diaz Fanning's obsession with Smith Bradbury and his attempt to force her to leave her husband, leading to a deadly confrontation.

phases.name: Initial Investigation
phases.objective: Gather initial clues and speak with key witnesses at Baker Street and Riding Thorpe Manor.

phases.name: Expanding the Search
phases.objective: Explore additional locations and uncover more clues about the mysterious messages and the individuals involved.

phases.name: The Farm Connection
phases.objective: Investigate Elrige’s Farm and gather evidence to connect Diaz Fanning to the crime.

phases.name: Final Confrontation
phases.objective: Confront the culprit and piece together the final elements of the mystery to solve the case.

eastwood_rapp.persona: Sharp, observant, and methodical. Speaks with a mix of dry wit and intellectual superiority. Prefers to let others draw their own conclusions before revealing his deductions.

knowledge_about_others.dr_burrows: Trusts Burrows implicitly and values his companionship, though he often teases him for his lack of observational skills.
knowledge_about_others.barr_bradbury: Respects Bradbury’s integrity and concern for his wife but finds his naivety about her past frustrating.
knowledge_about_others.diaz_fanning: Views Fanning as a dangerous and obsessive criminal who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals.

eastwood_rapp.abilities: Master of deduction, cryptography, and forensic analysis. Skilled at piecing together seemingly unrelated clues to form a coherent narrative.

required_evidence: Slips of paper with dancing men drawings

Rapp will confirm Diaz Fanning’s identity and criminal background, increasing his determination to apprehend him.
Rapp will confront Diaz Fanning, using the evidence to force a confession and reveal the full truth of the case.

dr_burrows.persona: Curious, loyal, and occasionally exasperated by Rapp’s secrecy. Acts as the player’s guide, asking questions and providing context for Rapp’s deductions.

knowledge_about_others.eastwood_rapp: Admires Rapp’s intellect but is often baffled by his methods until the final reveal.
knowledge_about_others.barr_bradbury: Sympathizes with Bradbury’s plight and is horrified by the tragedy that befalls him.

knowledge_about_others.smith_bradbury: Loves his wife deeply and trusts her implicitly, though he is troubled by her secrecy and fear.
knowledge_about_others.diaz_fanning: Unaware of Fanning’s existence until the messages appear, but grows increasingly suspicious and fearful as the case progresses.

barr_bradbury.secret: He is unaware of the true nature of his wife’s past and the identity of the man behind the dancing men messages. His trust in Smith blinds him to the danger until it is too late.

knowledge_about_others.diaz_fanning: Fears Fanning and is desperate to keep him from harming her husband. She knows his true nature and the threat he poses.

smith_bradbury.secret: She was once engaged to Diaz Fanning and fled America to escape his influence. She has been receiving threats from him in the form of the dancing men messages and is terrified of what he might do.

required_evidence: Slips of paper with dancing men drawings
conditional_behaviors.reaction: Smith will grow visibly distressed when the messages are discussed, refusing to explain their meaning or her connection to them.

diaz_fanning.persona: Charismatic, aggressive, and manipulative. Speaks with a mix of charm and menace, often justifying his actions as being in the name of love. His obsession with Smith is evident in every word.

knowledge_about_others.smith_bradbury: Claims to love Smith and believes he has a right to her. Views her marriage to Bradbury as a betrayal and is determined to win her back at any cost.
knowledge_about_others.barr_bradbury: Sees Bradbury as an obstacle to his happiness and harbors deep resentment toward him, though he claims he never intended to kill him.

diaz_fanning.secret: He is the one sending the dancing men messages to Smith, threatening her and demanding she leave her husband. His obsession led him to confront Bradbury, resulting in a deadly shootout.

Fanning will confess to the confrontation with Bradbury but will insist he never intended to harm Smith. His confession will reveal the full truth of the case.

knowledge_about_others.eastwood_rapp: Initially views Rapp as an eccentric but comes to respect his deductive abilities and insights.
knowledge_about_others.diaz_fanning: Sees Fanning as a dangerous criminal and is determined to bring him to justice.

inspector_vance.abilities: Skilled in police procedure, evidence collection, and interrogation. Provides legal authority and support to Rapp’s investigation.

conditional_behaviors.reaction: Vance will express surprise at the evidence of a third shooter and will work with Rapp to piece together the sequence of events.
Vance will recognize the significance of the hand-bag as evidence of Fanning’s attempt to bribe Smith and will use it to build a case against him.

mrs_king.persona: Loyal, observant, and protective of the Bradbury family. Speaks with a mix of warmth and caution, often downplaying her knowledge to avoid gossip.

knowledge_about_others.barr_bradbury: Respects Bradbury and is horrified by his death. She feels a sense of responsibility for the household and its safety.

mrs_king.secret: She is aware of the tension in the household and has noticed Smith’s fear, but she does not know the cause. She is also aware of the hand-bag but does not know its significance.

conditional_behaviors.reaction: Mrs. King will admit to seeing the hand-bag but will claim she does not know where it came from or who it belongs to.

caplan.persona: Young, nervous, and eager to please. Speaks quickly and often jumps to conclusions. She is easily flustered but means well.

knowledge_about_others.smith_bradbury: Admires Smith but is puzzled by her behavior and the strange messages. She wants to help but is afraid of overstepping.
knowledge_about_others.barr_bradbury: Respects Bradbury and is devastated by his death. She feels guilty for not doing more to prevent the tragedy.

caplan.secret: She has seen the dancing men messages and is curious about them but has not mentioned them to anyone for fear of causing trouble. She also knows about the trampled flower-bed but does not connect it to the messages.

required_evidence: The trampled flower-bed and footprints outside the study window

riding_thorpe_manor.description: A grand, old manor house with oak-paneled halls and high windows. The atmosphere is one of quiet elegance, but tension lingers in the air. The study, tool-house, and garden are key areas of interest.
riding_thorpe_manor.setting: The manor is a sprawling, centuries-old estate with a mix of Tudor and Georgian architecture. The interior is warm and inviting, with rich wood paneling, antique furniture, and portraits of the Bradbury ancestors lining the walls. The garden outside is meticulously maintained, with a sundial and a black tool-house near the study window.
clues: The trampled flower-bed and footprints outside the study window indicate an intruder's presence
The timing and sequence of the gunshots (two nearly simultaneous) imply a confrontation

people.name: Smith Bradbury
people.description: A tall, elegant woman with a pale face and haunted eyes. She moves quietly and speaks softly, often avoiding direct answers.
people.notes: Smith is deeply troubled by the dancing men messages and her past. She is terrified of Diaz Fanning and the danger he poses to her husband.

people.name: Mrs. King
people.description: A stout, middle-aged woman with a kind face and a no-nonsense demeanor. She is always busy with household tasks.
people.notes: Mrs. King is loyal to the Bradburys and is aware of the tension in the household but does not know the cause.

people.name: Caplan
people.description: A young, slender woman with a nervous energy. She is often seen hurrying about her duties.
people.notes: Caplan is curious about the dancing men messages but is afraid to ask questions. She is eager to help but easily flustered.

objects.name: Study Desk
objects.description: A large, oak desk cluttered with papers, books, and writing implements. A candle sits in a brass holder, casting a flickering light.
objects.notes: The desk is where Barr Bradbury spent much of his time. It may contain clues related to the case.

objects.name: Window Sash
objects.description: A wooden window sash with a small bullet hole near the bottom. The glass is intact, but the wood is splintered.
objects.notes: The bullet hole suggests a third shooter was present outside the study during the confrontation.

objects.name: Hand-bag
objects.description: A small, crocodile-skin hand-bag with silver clasps. It contains a large sum of money.
objects.notes: The hand-bag suggests an attempt at bribery or payment, likely connected to Diaz Fanning.

objects.name: Revolver
objects.description: A small, pearl-handled revolver with two empty barrels. It is the murder weapon.
objects.notes: The revolver was used in the confrontation between Bradbury and Fanning. Its ejector and the recovered cartridge confirm a third shot was fired.

baker_street.description: A cozy, cluttered apartment filled with books, chemical apparatuses, and strange artifacts. The air is thick with the smell of tobacco and experiments. This is where Eastwood Rapp resides and conducts his investigations.
baker_street.setting: The apartment is a mix of Victorian elegance and scientific chaos. A large bay window overlooks Baker Street, and the walls are lined with bookshelves filled with volumes on crime, chemistry, and cryptography. A chemical apparatus bubbles in the corner, and a Persian slipper holds Rapp’s tobacco.
clues: The dancing men hieroglyphics convey a coded message
The symbol 'XXX' (or variations) repeatedly stands for the letter 'E'

people.name: Eastwood Rapp
people.description: A tall, thin man with sharp features and piercing eyes. He moves with a quiet intensity and speaks in a measured, deliberate tone.
people.notes: Rapp is a master detective with a keen mind for puzzles and cryptography. He is deeply invested in solving the case of the dancing men.

people.name: Dr. Burrows
people.description: A stout, genial man with a round face and a friendly demeanor. He is often seen observing Rapp’s methods with curiosity.
people.notes: Burrows is Rapp’s loyal friend and chronicler. He provides context and asks questions that help the player understand the case.

objects.name: Chemical Apparatus
objects.description: A complex setup of glass tubes, beakers, and burners, bubbling with a malodorous liquid. Rapp uses it for his experiments.
objects.notes: The apparatus is a constant presence in Rapp’s apartment, reflecting his scientific interests.

objects.name: Slips of Paper with Dancing Men Drawings
objects.description: Several small slips of paper covered in strange, childlike drawings of dancing men. The figures seem to form a coded message.
objects.notes: These slips are the key to deciphering the dancing men code and uncovering the truth behind the messages.

objects.name: Rapp’s Notebook
objects.description: A leather-bound notebook filled with Rapp’s observations, deductions, and sketches. It is his most prized possession.
objects.notes: The notebook contains Rapp’s notes on the dancing men case, including his attempts to decipher the code.

contains.name: Cablegram from Ledger Eisenberg
contains.description: A cablegram confirming the identity and criminal background of Diaz Fanning.
contains.notes: The cablegram provides crucial information about Fanning’s past and his connection to Smith Bradbury.

tool_house.description: A small, black wooden shed located near the garden of Riding Thorpe Manor. The door is covered in strange chalk drawings of dancing men.
tool_house.setting: The tool-house is a simple, utilitarian structure with a sloped roof and a single door. The garden around it is well-tended, with flower-beds and a sundial nearby. The chalk drawings on the door are the most striking feature.
clues: The word 'NEVER' in the dancing men messages indicates a refusal or warning

objects.name: Tool-House Door
objects.description: A black wooden door covered in chalk drawings of dancing men. The drawings seem to form a message.
objects.notes: The door is where the dancing men messages first appeared, drawn in chalk. It is a key piece of evidence in the case.

objects.name: Chalk
objects.description: A piece of white chalk, likely used to draw the dancing men on the tool-house door.
objects.notes: The chalk provides a clue to how the messages were created and who might have drawn them.

study.description: A small, book-lined chamber at Riding Thorpe Manor. The room is dimly lit, with a writing-table facing a window that looks out onto the garden. The air is thick with the smell of gunpowder.
study.setting: The study is a cozy but cluttered room, with bookshelves lining three walls and a large oak desk near the window. The window sash has a bullet hole, and the floor is scuffed from the recent struggle. A candle on the desk provides the only light.
clues: The bullet hole in the window sash suggests a third shooter outside the study

objects.name: Writing Table
objects.description: A large oak table covered in papers, books, and writing implements. A candle flickers in a brass holder.
objects.notes: The table is where Barr Bradbury worked and where the confrontation likely took place.

objects.name: Third Cartridge
objects.description: A small, brazen cartridge ejected from the revolver. It was found in the garden outside the study window.
objects.notes: The cartridge confirms that a third shot was fired during the confrontation, suggesting the presence of a third person.

elriges_farm.description: A lonely, isolated farmhouse located a few miles from Riding Thorpe Manor. The farm is quiet and unassuming, but it holds dark secrets.
elriges_farm.setting: The farm is a simple, weather-beaten structure surrounded by fields and hedgerows. The interior is sparsely furnished, with a few rooms for the farmer and his lodgers. The atmosphere is one of quiet isolation.
clues: The revolver's ejector and the recovered cartridge confirm a third shot was fired

people.name: Diaz Fanning
people.description: A tall, swarthy man with a bristling black beard and a confident, aggressive demeanor. He carries himself like a man used to getting his way.
people.notes: Fanning is the culprit behind the dancing men messages and the deadly confrontation at Riding Thorpe Manor. He is obsessed with Smith Bradbury and will stop at nothing to win her back.

objects.name: Farmer’s Desk
objects.description: A simple wooden desk in the farmhouse. It is cluttered with papers, tools, and farming ledgers.
objects.notes: The desk may contain clues about Fanning’s stay at the farm and his connection to the Bradburys.

north_walsham_train_station.setting: The station is a modest but well-maintained building with a platform, ticket office, and waiting area. The air is filled with the sound of trains and the chatter of passengers. A large clock hangs above the platform, marking the time.
